Subject: Redwood Private VPC - network & airgap feasibility (post-call recap)

Hi Tim / Mallory / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

1) Summary of ask: Acme wants a Private (VPC) deployment of Redwood with the option for an air-gapped installation in a future phase. Primary concerns: control plane networking, egress/ingress restrictions, and packaged offline updates.

2) What Redwood can do (short):
- Private deployment: customer-hosted control plane with optional managed control plane (we can run in your VPC via a peered/proxy pattern).
- Air-gap support: we provide an airgap installer bundle and a documented workflow for offline updates (we'll validate the installer against your policies).
- Networking: minimal outbound calls (license/control checks) can be proxied; we can also operate with a fully offline control plane depending on the PoC scope.

3) Proposed PoC tests (we recommend starting with networking + control plane behavior):
- Basic connectivity test: validate required ports and egress endpoints (we'll provide a short CSV).
- Control plane mode test: set up a staging VPC with our private runtime and validate model loads + latency.
- Air-gap install smoke test: install our airgap bundle in an isolated subnet and run a sample model inference.

4) Next steps / timeline:
- You: share a green-team contact (Priya, thanks for joining) and a list of firewall/egress constraints.
- Us: we'll send the network requirements CSV and an airgap installer stub + short runbook.
- Target: 1-week window for the basic connectivity test, then a 2-3 week PoC for the control plane + air-gap smoke.

I've attached a short product overview and the network requirements file to get started. Sarah from our engineering team (cc'd in follow-up) will coordinate the technical POC.

If that all looks good I can schedule the first connectivity test for next Tue/Wed.

Best,

Vanessa / team,

Draft checklist and PoC test plan below (happy to iterate):

A) Network requirements (basic):
- Outbound: allow HTTPS to the following hostnames for optional control plane telemetry (if running managed control plane): control.redwood.ai:443, updates.redwood.ai:443
- Recommended: allow proxy egress to the above endpoints via your corporate proxy.
- Ports (if fully private/on-prem): 443 outbound for optional license checks; no mandatory inbound internet ports.
- Internal: allow connectivity between runtime nodes on ports 5000-5100 (gRPC/tcp fallback) and 2200 (internal admin).

B) Control plane modes we support:
- Managed control plane (hosted by Redwood, peered via secure proxy): minimal egress required; easiest from a setup perspective.
- Customer-hosted control plane (recommended for strict data residency): our control plane components run in your VPC; we provide Helm charts and an image registry URL.
- Fully air-gapped control plane: we provide a tarball installer and offline registry export; customer must provide an internal registry and object store.

C) Airgap smoke test steps (high level):
- We supply: airgap-installer-v1.tar.gz (includes images, installer script, runbook).
- Customer: provision isolated subnet and internal registry; run installer; validate model artifact load and run 5 sample inferences.
- Success criteria: model loads within 3 minutes, 95th percentile latency < 250ms for sample input set.

D) PoC timeline (suggested):
- Day 0-2: connectivity test (verify proxy/firewall rules).
- Week 1-2: deploy customer-hosted control plane in staging VPC and validate model load.
- Week 3: air-gap smoke test in isolated environment (if requested).

Attachments: I'm attaching a CSV with the minimal host/port list and the airgap installer stub. I'll also prepare a short runbook for the installer.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao

Adding a short competitive note for procurement and the Acme security team. High-level bullets we can share: 

- Hyperscalers (AWS/GCP/Azure) pros: deep managed infra and marketplace procurement paths; cons: less flexible offline/airgap workflows and often higher sustained inference unit costs for predictable workloads.
- Redwood differentiators for this use-case:
  * Air-gapped installer & documented offline update flow (we supply signed images and an updater runbook).
  * Customer-hosted control plane option with the same API surface as our hosted product (makes cut-over easier).
  * Sensible unit economics for steady-state inference (reserved pools / quantization recommendations).
  * Ops tooling: rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) and token-level cost breakdowns to track spend in PoC.

Suggested collateral to attach for procurement: short pricing ballpark (one-pager), SOC2 report, and the product overview. I've attached the SOC2 PDF copy and a two-slide competitive summary.

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Marketing | Redwood Inference
